::: {#fig-flat-point}

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

### R

```{r}
#| label: flat-point-r
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Two panels. Left: the curve w cubed for w from -2 to 2, rising from -8 to 8
#|   and flattening at the origin, where a vermilion filled circle marks the flat
#|   point. Right: the curve w squared on the same range, a parabola with its
#|   lowest point at the origin and an open vermilion circle at w of 1, where the
#|   slope is 2 and the point is not flat.
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-width: 6
fp_w_ff <- seq(-2, 2, length.out = 201)
fp_cube_ff <- tibble::tibble(w = fp_w_ff, value = fp_w_ff^3, panel = "f(w) = w^3")
fp_square_ff <- tibble::tibble(w = fp_w_ff, value = fp_w_ff^2, panel = "h(w) = w^2")
fp_curves_ff <- rbind(fp_cube_ff, fp_square_ff)
fp_marks_w_ff <- c(0, 1)
fp_marks_panel_ff <- c("f(w) = w^3", "h(w) = w^2")
fp_marks_kind_ff <- c("flat point", "not a flat point")
fp_marks_ff <- tibble::tibble(
  w = fp_marks_w_ff, value = fp_marks_w_ff,
  panel = fp_marks_panel_ff, kind = fp_marks_kind_ff
)
fp_aes_ff <- ggplot2::aes(w, value)
fp_marks_aes_ff <- ggplot2::aes(shape = kind)
fp_shapes_ff <- c("flat point" = 16, "not a flat point" = 1)
ggplot2::ggplot(fp_curves_ff, fp_aes_ff) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(colour = "#0072B2") +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    data = fp_marks_ff, mapping = fp_marks_aes_ff,
    colour = "#D55E00", size = 3
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(values = fp_shapes_ff) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y") +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "w", y = NULL, shape = NULL)
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: flat-point-python
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Two panels. Left: the curve w cubed for w from -2 to 2, rising from -8 to 8
#|   and flattening at the origin, where a vermilion filled circle marks the flat
#|   point. Right: the curve w squared on the same range, a parabola with its
#|   lowest point at the origin and an open vermilion circle at w of 1, where the
#|   slope is 2 and the point is not flat.
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-width: 6
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

fp_w_ff = np.linspace(-2, 2, 201)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(6, 3.5), layout="constrained")
axes[0].plot(fp_w_ff, fp_w_ff**3, color="#0072B2")
axes[0].plot(0, 0, "o", color="#D55E00", markersize=8, label="flat point")
axes[0].set_title("f(w) = w^3")
axes[1].plot(fp_w_ff, fp_w_ff**2, color="#0072B2")
axes[1].plot(1, 1, "o", color="#D55E00", markerfacecolor="none",
             markersize=8, label="not a flat point")
axes[1].set_title("h(w) = w^2")
for ax in axes:
    ax.set_xlabel("w")
    ax.legend(loc="upper center")
plt.show()
```

:::

The [functions](functions.qmd#def-function) of @exm-flat-point.
The [slope](algebra.qmd#def-slope) of $f(w) = w^3$ is $0$ at $w = 0$, so $0$ is a [flat point](#def-flat-point),
yet $f$ keeps rising through it.
The slope of $h(w) = w^2$ at $w = 1$ is $2$, so $1$ is not a flat point.

:::
